terms.label: Series 76 Electric Actuators
terms.definition: The data provided pertains to the Series 76, a line of heavy-duty electric actuators. These devices are critical components in industrial automation, used to remotely open, close, or precisely control valves and dampers in a wide range of applications, from HVAC systems to industrial processing plants.

terms.label: Understanding the Data Tables
terms.definition: The provided tables contain the Electrical Data for the Series 76 actuators. This data is essential for engineers and technicians to select the correct actuator model for a specific application based on power availability and performance requirements. The data is segmented based on several key criteria:

terms.label: Weatherproof
terms.definition: Designed for general industrial use, protected against dust, rain, and environmental elements (compliant with CSA, CE, & UKCA standards).

terms.label: Explosionproof
terms.definition: Built with a more robust enclosure to be safely operated in hazardous environments where flammable gases or dust may be present (compliant with CSA, IECEx/ATEX standards).

terms.label: 24V AC/DC
terms.definition: Low voltage direct or alternating current.

terms.label: On/Off
terms.definition: The actuator operates in two positions: fully open or fully closed.

terms.label: Modulating
terms.definition: The actuator can be controlled to stop at any point in its 90-degree rotation, allowing for precise flow control.

terms.label: Base Part Number
terms.definition: The unique identifier for each actuator model (e.g., 761A00-11380000/A).

terms.label: Output Torque
terms.definition: The rotational force the actuator can produce, measured in in-lbs (inch-pounds) and Nm (Newton-meters). This is a primary performance metric.

terms.label: Duty Cycle (S4%)
terms.definition: The percentage of time the actuator can be in operation over a given cycle without overheating.

terms.label: Operating Speed (Sec)
terms.definition: The time it takes for the actuator to complete a full 90-degree turn. For AC models, this can vary based on the power frequency (50 Hz vs. 60 Hz).

terms.label: Full Load Current (FLA)
terms.definition: The electric current (in Amps) drawn by the motor under its maximum rated load.

terms.label: Locked Rotor Current (LRA)
terms.definition: The current drawn by the motor at startup, which is significantly higher than the FLA.

terms.label: Motor Power
terms.definition: The power rating of the internal motor, measured in Watts.
